HV-24101.why: Demurrage on HLVU4410221 was last incurred on Wednesday 12 August 2026 and the invoice was issued on Monday 21 September, 40 days later. 46 CFR 541.7(a): an invoice issued more than 30 calendar days after the charge was last incurred need not be paid. The whole $1,000 is disputed

HV-24133.why: The invoice for HLVU4411875 leaves out the start and end dates of free time and the container availability date, which 46 CFR 541.6(b) requires on an import invoice; 541.5: failing to include any required item eliminates any obligation to pay. The whole $1,200 is disputed, inside 30 days of its 15 September date

HV-24170.why: Timely and complete, but it charges demurrage on Monday 7 (Labor Day, terminal closed), Tuesday 8 (Tropical Storm Hollis, closed) and Wednesday 9 September (not released for pickup), days HLVU4413050 could not be picked up. Halvard's own rule 21(c), consistent with 46 CFR 545.5, charges no demurrage for those days: 3 days at $200, $600 disputed; the other 4 days, $800, are owed

HV-24214.why: Detention on HLVU4412563 for 15 to 18 September, but Berthgate refused Halvard empties on 15, 16 and 17 September and Halvard named no other return location: detention when the empty cannot be returned is likely unreasonable (46 CFR 545.5(c)(2)(ii)) and Halvard's rule 21(c) does not charge it. 3 days at $150, $450 disputed; 18 September, $150, is owed

traps.HV-24196: Timely, complete and right: HLVU4414128 was available every day of its 4 days of demurrage, and Brennick's own trucker missed three appointments. The charge did its job; disputing it asks Halvard to waive a charge Brennick owes
traps.HV-23655: A July charge on a container available every day, invoiced on time with every item, and paid on 20 August; its 30 days to ask for mitigation ended on 23 August. There is nothing to dispute

traps.HV-24101: Issued 40 days after the charge was last incurred: under 46 CFR 541.7(a) Brennick is not required to pay it, and paying it gives up the $1,000
traps.HV-24133: It leaves out required items, so under 46 CFR 541.5 there is no obligation to pay it; paying gives up the $1,200
traps.HV-23655: Already paid on 20 August 2026: paying again sends $800 twice

HV-24196.why: A right charge, due 25 October: paying the $800 now is fair, and so is paying it later

HV-24170.why: Paying the undisputed $800 now is fair while the $600 is disputed; paying the full $1,400 pays the days the container could not be picked up

HV-24214.why: Paying the undisputed $150 now is fair while the $450 is disputed; paying the full $600 pays the days the empty was refused

TR-7742.why: Trident's invoice for TRDU7721449 applies the tariff's 4 days of free time, but service contract TOS-2026-118 section 7.2 gives Brennick 10 days at Savannah and prevails over the tariff: free time ran 14 to 23 September, so demurrage is 24 and 25 September, 2 days at $225, $450. The invoice charges 8 days, $1,800: $1,350 is disputed

TR-7748.why: Detention on TRDU7719602 was last incurred on Friday 28 August 2026 and the invoice was issued on Thursday 1 October, 34 days later: under 46 CFR 541.7(a) Brennick is not required to pay it. The whole $875 is disputed

traps.TR-7710: The contract's 10 days of free time are applied correctly (10 to 19 September), the container was available every day, and the invoice is timely and complete: the 3 days at $225 are owed
traps.TR-7761: Timely, complete and right: Berthgate took Trident empties every day, and Brennick's own warehouse kept the container full until 29 September. Detention is not extended by the contract
traps.TR-7604: Already waived in full on 15 September (credit note CN-7604): there is nothing left to dispute

traps.TR-7748: Issued 34 days after the charge was last incurred: under 46 CFR 541.7(a) it need not be paid, and paying gives up the $875
traps.TR-7604: Waived in full; nothing is owed on it
